text: Writing clean code is a skill that benefits both you and your team. The most important principle is readability; code should be easy for others to understand at a glance, not just for a computer to execute. This starts with good naming conventions: use clear, descriptive names for variables and functions, such as `calculateTotalPrice` instead of `ctp`. Also, break your code into small, focused functions that each do one thing well. This not only makes the logic simpler to follow but also makes testing easier. Ultimately, clean code ensures maintainability, meaning it can be updated and fixed without causing unexpected problems, saving time and frustration in the long run.
